name: Grounded goal agent
description: The one engine that takes a person's goal from question to finished work: it answers from their own material, carries out what they ask, and runs their queued tasks, configured per consumer rather than rebuilt for each.
purpose: Keeps a person's or team's goals moving by answering from their own material, carrying out requested changes, and running queued work to a written standard.
approach: Grounds each answer and action in the person's own goals and material, and reports every task result against the goal it serves.
out_of_scope: Rendering a chat interface, storing goal data, holding any one organization's names, rules or data, running as a hosted service, and taking decisions that belong to a person.
milestones: 1. Queued tasks meet their written goal without human rework, at a cost per task the operator accepts. 2. Realistic chat turns pass their rubric on grounded facts, right handling and exact changes, at a cost per passing turn the operator accepts. 3. No unrequested write is made, no requested write is missing, and no human-only step is taken without a person. 4. No item from another user, team or quest reaches a prompt or store. 5. Every solution has a current measured result, and its selection follows that result. 6. Each consumer writes no glue of its own and copies no engine code into itself.
knowledge: Agent loop research (reason and act, plan and execute, verification against a written goal); retrieval-augmented generation and context selection; evaluation of language-model systems; Quest's model of quests, goals, notes, asks and AI tasks; the operating principle "AI acts first, humans confirm"; Joshua's evolvable structure that optimizes intent.
measures_of_success: People's goals move through delegated work; tasks and replies need no correction; operators accept the cost; Joshua can steer by reviewing metrics without needing to read code. Standing conditions: Chat turns that pass their rubric (grounded facts, right handling, exact changes) at a cost per passing turn the operator accepts; queued tasks that meet their written goal; no unrequested writes and no human-only step taken alone; no data across scope; every part measured and selected by its metric.
parameters: One configuration per lane: the consumer's adapters (retrieval, cards, conversations, escalation, deep runner), model tiers and providers, personas, budgets and schedules, and the implementation selected for each swappable solution.
inputs: A person's message or a queued task, the quest and goal it concerns, and the sources the adapters reach.
outputs: A reply, a task result reported against its goal, a decision-request for a person, or files and records changed as requested.
effects: Writes to Quest and other systems through their APIs and tools; model and search spend; context cards and conversation memory kept for later turns.
usage_notes: Two entry points share one brain: the importable core (`Orchestrator`) for chat and other hosts, and the runner (a lane that polls, claims, runs, escalates and reports) for queued work. A terminal chat drives the same brain. Every specific comes through configuration; nothing about a consumer is built in.

name: Justified model calls
description: Keeps every model call tied to a registered prompt spec with an owner solution and metric, so a call stays only while its measured value outweighs its cost and time.
purpose: Gives an operator a known value, cost and time for every model call, so spend and latency go only to prompts that earn them and a cheaper or faster option is not missed.
approach: Every prompt is a registered PromptSpec (id, owner solution, metric, tier, cache layer, output schema, no-em-dash rule) in core/prompt_specs.py. One enforced call path, checked by tests/test_prompt_specs.py with a shrinking baseline, admits only registered prompts. A per-call ablation drops or downgrades the call and checks the owner metric.
out_of_scope: Choosing the model tier for a turn (choose-a-model-tier), the daily budget (track-usage-and-cost), and the content of any one prompt.
milestones: 1. Every call site is a registered spec and the baseline of unregistered sites is empty. 2. Each spec has a per-call ablation row on production-shaped cases. 3. Each spec has a budget for cost, tokens and latency set from the value its owner metric shows.
knowledge: Dictated by Joshua 2026-10-28 and recorded as given; not built beyond the registry and the enforcement test, so the metric is unmeasured. Known today: the call sites still unregistered are listed in tests/prompt_spec_baseline.txt; spend-weighted value not computed.
measures_of_success: The metric is read from recorded rows without invented readings. Standing conditions: Never invent a reading. Label rows taken from eval traces until production data exists.
parameters: The bar (0.8) and each prompt's own budget for cost, tokens and latency.
inputs: The per-call usage records tagged with the spec id (quest_ai_runner/the_world/model_plumbing/spend/usage.py) and production-shaped eval cases (quest_ai_prod_examples shapes).
outputs: A per-prompt table and the share of average model spend that is justified.
effects: No model call of its own except the ablation runs, which are paid and run only by decision with a budget.
usage_notes: Selected today: spec_registry. The ablation arm is proposed and not built.
